newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - JAN 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - JAN 2.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--Deputy Foreign Minister Christos Rozakis is reported to be considering quitting if there is no joint commitment from Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos on the planning and course of foreign policy at a meeting to be chaired by Prime Minister Costas Simitis on January 9. Rozakis is reported to have said his post has harmed his position as an independent expert, following repeated attacks from former defence minister Gerasimos Arsenis and current minister Akis Tsohatzopoulos.
--British Foreign Office archives: British services were so busy with the activities of George and Andreas Papandreou in 1966 that they failed to see the military coup coming.
--Criticism over bad planning and organisation failed to dampen Thessaloniki's New Year celebrations that saw in its term as Cultural Capital of Europe.
--The testimony of the lone survivor of the Dystos capsize reveals that the vessel sailed from Volos with problems. Twenty were lost in the tragedy.
--The estimated 400,000 illegal immigrants will have a chance at legalising their presence in Greece under a new presidential decree that will issue them a residence permit.
--Determined to implement the new austere rule of one appointment for every five departures in the public sector, only 10,000 new appointments are provided for in 1997.
--Some 18,000 Greeks played one billion drachmas at casinos on New Year's Eve.

--A European-supported US initiative on Greek-Turkish differences is expected to be announced by March, former US ambassador to Greece Monteagle Sterns says. Sterns visited Nicosia and Athens in November on a fact-finding visit.
--A police raid on a rave party in an Athens district last night netted 32 arrests and a susbtantial amount of cocaine and Ecstasy pills.

--Athens Mayor Dimitris Avramopoulos throws down the gauntlet to opposition New Democracy leader Miltiades Evert, in what is his first public comment on developments in the conservative opposition party. "Leaders do not come out of congress: the people choose them," the enormously popular mayor says.
--A crop of seven newborn babies arrived to celebrate the New Year.
